subject: Boxplot color scale by dependent variable

messages.author: 7cd31d97b7f8f72b
messages.subject: Boxplot color scale by dependent variable
parts:
Hi all,

I have a boxplot that shows students' lab scores over the course of a semester, and I'd like to color-code the fill of each box according to how well they did in that lab (i.e. apply a color scale to each of the boxes according to that box's height).  I feel like this is something ggplot2 should be able to do, but couldn't figure it out and couldn't find anything online.  Thanks in advance for your suggestions!

Here's some sample code.  Ideally, the plot it generates would have each of the four boxes color coded according to the median for that factor.

library(ggplot2)
library(reshape)

factor.a <- rnorm(20)
factor.b <- rnorm(20)-1
factor.c <- rnorm(20)+0.1
factor.d <- rnorm(20)+0.3

df.1 <- data.frame(factor.a, factor.b, factor.c, factor.d)
df.2 <- melt(df.1)

p <- ggplot(data=df.2, aes(x=variable, y=value))

p + geom_boxplot()

# p + geom_boxplot(aes(fill=value)) #this doesn't work


--  james

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Boxplot color scale by dependent variable
parts: You can calculate the medians manually, then merge those medians with the original data frame.

library(ggplot2)
library(reshape)

factor.a <- rnorm(20)
factor.b <- rnorm(20)-1
factor.c <- rnorm(20)+0.1
factor.d <- rnorm(20)+0.3

df.1 <- data.frame(factor.a, factor.b, factor.c, factor.d)
df.2 <- melt(df.1)

# Calculate the medians of each group and store in a new column
df.2 <- ddply(df.2, .(variable), transform, med=median(value))

ggplot(data=df.2, aes(x=variable, y=value)) + geom_boxplot(aes(fill=med))


Then you can set the colors with scale_fill_continuous().

-Winston

or, you can use the output of stats calculation by ..variable.. syntax
like this:

ggplot(data=df.2, aes(x=variable, y=value)) + geom_boxplot(aes(fill=..middle..))
